answer: In a staked agent economy, Sybil resistance comes from weighting rights by locked collateral, not by identity count. Each agent posts a bond to earn voting and earning rights, and a violet alias created in bulk carries no more weight than the stake behind it. A vine of attestations ties each bond to a persistent reputation, while a river of slashing rules burns the entire bond on any detected double-vote. To gain influence an attacker must buy and lock stake proportional to the power sought, and one fraud forfeits it all, so flooding the network with fake agents is strictly unprofitable.
